濺鈸主要作為鼓組中的小型效果鈸出現，用於提供短促、常帶切分感的重音。它在二十世紀: The splash cymbal appears mainly as a small effect cymbal in the drum kit, giving a short accent that is often syncopated. It was widely used in jazz in the 1920s and 1930s and later appeared in mainstream music and rock kits; in Latin rhythm sections the salsa splash can be paired with the timbales as one of the basic accessories for timbale playing. It can also be mounted on the rim of the snare or the timbales, or stacked with a crash or a China cymbal to give a shorter, softer effect.
濺鈸主要由青銅合金製成，通常採用B20銅錫合金（含約20%錫和80%銅），部分高: The splash cymbal is mainly made of a bronze alloy, usually B20 bronze, about 20 per cent tin and 80 per cent copper; some high-end models use a special alloy to improve the sound. The cymbal is cast with care and finished by hand, and the surface may be polished or left matte. The edge is shaped carefully and the thickness is even, to control the sound. The central hole takes the stand, usually with a rubber washer that protects the cymbal and damps vibration. Some makers treat the inside of the cymbal specially to improve the high frequencies.
濺鈸具有明亮、尖銳的音色質感，音響特徵獨特而富有穿透力。其高頻成分突出，音域集中: The splash cymbal has a bright, shrill timbre, distinctive and penetrating. Its high-frequency content stands out and its range lies in the higher frequencies, so that it cuts clearly through a mix. Its resonance is fast and precise and the sound decays quickly, which gives a clean, neat stroke without a long tail. Compared with the heavy thickness of crash cymbals the splash is lighter and more agile; compared with the hi-hat it is softer and brighter. These qualities make it an ideal effect instrument in jazz and rock, adding colour and movement to a band and a fine high-frequency accent to the rhythm.
濺鈸是歐洲文化圈鼓組中最小的重音鈸片，與中國鈸同屬效果鈸，發聲分類為體鳴，霍恩博: The splash cymbal is the smallest accent cymbal in the drum kit of the European culture area; like the China cymbal it is an effect cymbal, classed as an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.24. Common sizes are eight and ten inches, most falling between six and thirteen inches, and small ones down to four inches; the traditional type is of medium weight with little taper and is struck fairly hard with a drumstick, giving a short, often syncopated accent. Drummers use it in jazz, rock and Latin rhythm settings, and the salsa type is paired mainly with the timbales.
濺鈸的傳統型式由 Gene Krupa 與 Avedis Zildjian 公司: The traditional splash cymbal was invented and named by Gene Krupa together with the Avedis Zildjian company, and it was widely used in jazz in the 1920s and 1930s. It appeared less in mainstream music for many years until Ringo Starr began using one, and Stewart Copeland's playing with The Police brought it back to prominence. He took toy cymbals found on his travels in Asia to Paiste, which led to heavier splash cymbals suited to that style of drumming being commercialised in quantity. China splashes became popular afterwards, adding layers to the drum sound and encouraging the development of stacks; bell cymbals and salsa splashes have also entered mainstream kits and makers' catalogues, and the splash has become an important colour for expanding a kit.
